summary: Spot 1 is most likely monolayer WS2 (moderate confidence; PL or AFM needed to confirm) and spot 2 is thick, bulk-like WS2. Spot 1 has A1g at 417.3 cm-1, an A1g-E separation of about 62 cm-1, a strongly enhanced 2LA(M) (2LA/A1g height about 2.2) and a strong Si signal. Spot 2 has A1g at 420.1 cm-1, a separation of about 64.7 cm-1, a weak 2LA (ratio about 0.46) and a Si signal about 10 times weaker. A bilayer is not excluded by Raman alone.

observations.finding: A1g hardens by 2.8 cm-1 from spot 1 to spot 2 while E stays at 355.3-355.4 cm-1, so the A1g-E separation grows from 62.0 to 64.7 cm-1. This is the thickness trend, with spot 1 near the monolayer value and spot 2 bulk-like.
observations.source: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013), layer-dependence of E and A1g; Zhao et al., Nanoscale 5, 9677 (2013) (recalled from memory, not checked)

observations.finding: The 2LA(M) mode is strongly enhanced at spot 1, a double-resonance effect near the A exciton at 514.5 nm that is typical of monolayer WS2, and is much weaker at spot 2.
observations.evidence: 2LA/A1g height about 2.2 (area about 4.4) at spot 1 vs about 0.46 (area about 0.9) at spot 2
observations.source: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013), Fig. 3

observations.finding: The Si substrate signal is about 10 times stronger through the island than at the thick spot, consistent with a thin, nearly transparent layer at spot 1 and an absorbing thick layer at spot 2.
observations.evidence: Si 520.8 cm-1 area about 6770 (spot 1) vs about 660 (spot 2)

properties.name: defect_level
properties.value: not determinable; no direct defect markers (LA(M) at 176 cm-1 is broad, FWHM 10-13 cm-1)

caveats: The 2LA(M) and E' peaks lie about 4 cm-1 apart and overlap strongly. Their fitted positions and areas are correlated, so the E position and the A-E separation are good to about +-1 cm-1 at best.
A1g is doping-sensitive and the modes shift with strain, so the A1g position alone can mimic a thickness change; substrate doping from SiO2 or CVD residue is possible.
The 2LA/A1g ratio depends on laser power, focus and substrate interference, so single-spectrum values should not be over-interpreted.
The monolayer-versus-bilayer call rests on small differences of about 1-2 cm-1, which is within the uncertainty of the fit; the Raman evidence for monolayer is therefore moderate.
The literature values were recalled from memory and not checked in this folder.
Wavenumber calibration was only checked against Si, which sits at 520.8-520.9 cm-1.
Spot 2 only indicates 'thick, bulk-like'; the layer count cannot be derived.
questions_for_user: Do you have a PL spectrum of spot 1? A strong A-exciton near 2.0 eV would confirm a monolayer.
Do you have AFM or optical-contrast data? A step height of about 0.7-0.8 nm would settle the thickness.
What were the laser power, grating and spectral resolution, to rule out heating and instrumental broadening?
Is the island uniform? Mapping the A1g position and the 2LA/A1g ratio would show it, and also show any strain or doping inhomogeneity.
What is the SiO2 thickness, which affects interference and the Si intensity?
citations: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013), Fig. 3
limits: The data cannot give an absolute layer count, only a relative one.
The data cannot tell strain from doping, or give the sign of strain.
The data cannot give the defect density.
The data cannot tell whether the island is uniform in thickness.
